subheading: MANAGEMENT OF HYPOGLYCEMIA IN A CHILD
subheading_corrected: MANAGEMENT OF HYPOGLYCEMIA IN A CHILD
text:
Management
- Early feeding in the first hour and glucose monitoring in the presence of risk factors is essential, for babies that cannot be fed, intravenous 10% dextrose-in-water should be administered at the maintenance dose (60-80 mL/kg/day for term babies, 70-100 mL/kg/day)on the first day. RBG should be checked at 1hour after commencement of infusion, 3-6 hourly for the first 24 hours and thereafter, 12 hourly.
- If RBG is < 2.6 mmol/L bolus of 4 mL/kg of 10% dextrose should be administered and maintenance infusion should be done at the rate of 8 mg/kg/minute.
- Measure blood glucose 30 minutes after the bolus of glucose:
- If between 45 mg/dL - 150 mg/dL, then measure blood glucose every three or four hours until it is 45 mg/dL or more on two consecutive measurements
- If it is < 45 mg/dL, repeat correction for hypoglycaemia, ensure IV fluid is going at prescribed rate, there may be need to increase GIR.
Ensure feeding is on-going if baby is fit to do so.\
Measure blood glucose after 30 minutes:
If still less than 45 mg/dL, repeat correction for hypoglycaemia, increase GIR, may go as high as 12 mg/kg/min and repeat blood glucose after 30 minutes,
– If still <45 mg/dL (refractory hypoglycaemia), suspect a serious underlying cause, investigate and treat. Consult a paediatric endocrinologist.
– If baby requires >12 mg/kg/min of glucose or more than 12.5%
dextrose concentration to maintain normoglycaemia, a central venous
line such as umbilical vein, central line of PICC should be inserted to
administer the higher concentration of glucose.

If hypoglycaemia persists despite 12 mg/kg/minute, serum insulin
should be measured and intravenous hydrocortisone 2.5-5 mg/kg
should be given 12 hourly.

If this step is ineffective, oral diazoxide 1.7-5 mg/kg 8 hourly with oral
chlorthiazide 10 mg/kg 12 hourly should be administered with close
monitoring for hypotension and dehydration.

In the extreme cases requiring more than 20 mg/kg/minute of glucose,
subcutaneous somatostatin octreotide 1 microgram/kg 4 hourly or
intramuscular glucagon 20 microgram/kg 6 hourly may be effective.

If hypoglycaemia persists with hyperinsulinism, partial
pancreatectomy is indicated
